boards.hardware: ESP32-S3-R8; 32 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM at 80 MHz; 360x360 ST77916 QSPI LCD, CST816 touch; GPIO7 battery latch, GPIO6 key; separate I2S microphone and speaker buses
boards.identify: Sugarat Button, also sold by SDGOODS as an electronic badge; native USB-C and a 360x360 round LCD. Uses the matching SDGOODS-ESP32S3 BSP pinout.
boards.use: Touch Factory launcher, WiFi setup, app installation/removal, cover carousel and Agent realtime voice
boards.notes: Brand Sugarat, model Button; the same hardware bought from SDGOODS uses this profile. Public names Sugarat, Button and SDGOODS all resolve here. The existing sdgoods-wifi profile, agent.status application ID and SDGOODS-ESP32S3 image compatibility model remain stable. The installable Agent Voice application now uses continuous realtime calls; GPIO6 starts/ends calls, and only its pull-down menu can exit to Launcher. Audio and real network calls await device acceptance. Platform product sdgoods (id 13, enterprise 0), confirmed by developer. Hotspot Sugarat-Button-XXXX. Factory build: --image-role factory. Uses sdgoods-v5 (physical layout 5, application ABI 3): 512 KiB recovery, two 3 MiB launcher_a/launcher_b images, a 10 MiB app_pool expanded to app_00..app_13, layout_journal, app_meta, isolated Agent Link settings and shared 13 MiB developer appdata. ESP-IDF boot subtypes and the vendor appdata label are preserved; native images require slot capability version 2 for the renamed partitions. Launcher B at the end of 32 MiB flash requires experimental 32-bit quad-flash cache mapping; hardware acceptance is pending. LCD GPIO12 supply enable is active low. Migrate from older layouts or vendor firmware with a full USB package; settings and installed applications are replaced. Hardware acceptance pending. Battery ADC uses GPIO8/ADC1_CH7 and a 3:1 divider, with calibrated sampling and the vendor 3.00-4.28 V percentage estimate; charging status is unknown (no documented input). QMI8658 six-axis sensor uses I2C address 0x6B. Agent_link Launcher downloads native apps and reviewed original SDGOODS pure applications from the operator's own backend catalog; vendor SDK return-to-launcher compatibility is enabled in source; hardware acceptance remains pending. Automatic rollback is disabled for unmodified vendor apps. Hold GPIO6 at power-on for three seconds to recover Factory (only OTA selection is cleared). Custom vendor bootloaders, fixed-layout applications and full-device updaters are outside this compatibility contract. Factory hardware pages provide battery/voltage, six-axis values, explicit speaker/microphone self-tests, saved brightness and confirmed sleep/off/restart. Audio recording stays in PSRAM and is freed after the test; PA is off when idle. TE has bounded interrupt synchronization with fallback; touch IRQ has polling fallback. Hardware behavior awaits device acceptance.
